source_context.quote: Ionic conductivity was characterized by impedance spectroscopy using an HP 4284A precision LCR meter (Hewlett-Packard, Japan). For the measurements, the OIPC sample was pressed by uniaxial compression at a pressure of 30 MPa, and silver powder electrodes were pressed onto the ends of the pellet also at 30 MPa. The measurements were performed using a two-electrode configuration in step-isotherm mode under the following conditions: low vacuum (residual pressure: 50 mTorr), a signal amplitude of 30 mV, and a frequency range of 3∙10¹ to 1∙10⁶ Hz.

Each molecule was placed in a cubic box with an edge length of 50 Å, and the OPLS4 50 force eld was applied to calculate the atomistic interactions.
The simulations were performed in the canonical NVT⁵⁷ ensemble at a temperature of 300 K and a pressure of 1 atm.
Temperature control was managed using the Nose–Hoover chain thermo- stat⁵⁸ with a relaxation time of 1.0 ps.
A cut-off radius of 9 Å was set for Coulomb interactions.
Each system underwent 100 ns of MD simulations, with trajectory frames saved at 100 ps inter- vals.
